paragraphs: R. Yehudah ben Pazi. “Rashi, Taanit, chapter 2, explains that Pazi was his mother's name and that he was R. Chiyya the Great's grandson.” Taanit 16a has R. Yehudah ben Pazi saying, etc., and Resh Lakish saying, etc., but I did not find this in Rashi there: he explained nothing of it. Tosafot, Bava Batra 149a, does trace R. Shimon ben Pazi through his mother; see R. Pazi and Mari bar Rachel above. I found in the Jerusalem Talmud R. Yehudah ben Pazi in R. Pazi's name (see there), so this is a sage's name, as also appears in the Zohar. See R. Yosi ben Pazi above. [One checked Sanhedrin witness names R. Pazi between Yehudah and R. Yochanan, and another omits him. The Zohar connects Yosi’s name to the return of a gold cup.] Shekalim 7:5; Mashilin, end of halakhah 2; Megillah 1:8: R. Yehudah ben Pazi taught, “Bar Dalya.” [The matching Megillah passage at 1:6:2 reads de-Barzilah, whereas the Beitzah parallel reads de-var Dalya.] End of Bameh Behemah and Beitzah 2:8: R. Yehudah ben Pazi of Bar Dalya, they told him. [The checked Bameh Behemah text reads Rav Dalya in this parallel.] End of Bameh Ishah: R. Yehudah ben Pazi taught, “Rav Dalya said”; and end of chapter 3. Jerusalem Berakhot, end of Ein Omdin, mishnah 5: R. Yehudah ben Pazi, in R. Elazar's name, says any priest who does not raise his hands transgresses a positive commandment. [At Berakhot 5:4:5, the rule specifies a priest who is present in the synagogue.] When old, R. Yehudah ben Pazi bound his head and stood behind a pillar; R. Elazar went outside; see there. Heilprin infers that Yehudah was a priest. [The checked Yerushalmi describes him at this point as weak.] Jerusalem Elu Megallechin, end of halakhah 5: R. Abba bar Kohen said before R. Yosi, R. Yehudah ben Pazi in R. Yochanan's name. R. Yosah stood with R. Yehudah ben Pazi and asked, “Did you hear this from your father?” He replied, “Father did not say that, but the brother of bar Nechemyah's wife died, and they asked him, etc.” R. Abba bar Kohen, in his name; see above. R. Acha. R. Aivu bar Nagri: Terumot 5:4 and HaYashen, halakhah 8. [The Terumot parallel is at 5:2:2 in the checked edition.] R. Immi, in his name: Jerusalem Rosh Hashanah, beginning of chapter 3. R. Bun, in his name: Jerusalem Kiddushin, beginning of chapter 1. Rav Huna. In R. Zeira's name: Jerusalem Rosh Hashanah, beginning of chapter 3. In R. Chunah Rabbah of Tzipporin's name: beginning of Kiddushin. R. Chizkiyah, in his name. In R. Chama, R. Oshaya's father's name: Jerusalem Sukkah, chapter 1, end of halakhah 1. R. Chananyah; R. Yehudah bar Titus; R. Yehudah bar Sison. R. Yudan of Cappadocia, in his name. In R. Yochanan's name; see above. In R. Yonatan's name. In R. Yosi son of R. Chanina's name. R. Yannai of Cappadocia. R. Yaakov bar Acha, in his name: Jerusalem Rosh Hashanah, beginning of chapter 3. R. Yaakov the Southerner, in his name. In R. Yirmeyah son of R. Chanina's name: Jerusalem Tomnin, end of halakhah 1. In R. Pazi's name; see above. In Rabbi's name: beginning of Shekalim. R. Shimon bar Abba.
